source: Canadian National Autism Foundation, cnaf.net/provinceres.html; each entry checked on its own website

entries.name: Nunavummi Disabilities Makinnasuaqtiit Society (NDMS)
entries.description: Nunavut's cross-disability organization, based in Iqaluit, for Nunavummiut with disabilities of all ages and their families. It offers individual and group advocacy, help applying for disability benefits such as the Disability Tax Credit and the Child First Initiative, employment supports, and accessible community activities.
entries.cost_note: The site does not mention cost.
entries.evidence: We provide advocacy, employment support, training, and accessibility services to help individuals, families, and organizations.
entries.notes: CNAF's link for this item goes to Nunavut Tunngavik Inc.'s About page (tunngavik.com/about), which does not mention NDMS; NDMS's own site is nuability.ca (its About page says NTI supported the group when it began in 1999, and it incorporated as a society in 2005). Contact details from the site footer; toll-free (877) 354-0916. Nunavut has no autism society of its own that could be found; NDMS describes itself as the territory's only cross-disability organization.

entries.name: Financial Assistance for Nunavut Students (FANS)
entries.description: The Government of Nunavut's financial help for Nunavut residents in full-time or part-time post-secondary programs, run by the Department of Education. Students with a disability can apply at any time during the academic year for a disability grant of up to $20,000.
entries.cost_note: Government grant and loan program; the page lists no application fee.
entries.evidence: Financial Assistance for Nunavut Students (FANS) is designed to ensure that financial need is not a barrier to higher education.
entries.notes: CNAF links to the old gov.nu.ca/family-services FANS page, which now redirects to this Department of Education page. Eligibility needs 12 months of Nunavut residency; the page describes 2025/2026 program changes and a coming name change. The FANS email on the page is hidden, and gov.nu.ca loaded only in some of fetch.py's modes (others got a Cloudflare check).

entries.name: Inuglugijaittuq: Inclusive Education (Nunavut Department of Education)
entries.description: The Nunavut Department of Education's inclusive education approach for students in Nunavut schools, with supports that increase from classroom practice to individual student support plans. Education support services include American Sign Language, assistive technology, instruction for students who are blind or have low vision or are Deaf or hard of hearing, educational psychology assessments, occupational therapy, speech language therapy and school mental health.
entries.cost_note: The page does not mention cost.
entries.evidence: Nunavut's model includes the provision of education support services: American Sign language, assistive technology for learning, Blind or Low Vision instruction, Deaf or Hard of Hearing instruction, educational psychology assessments, neurodiverse learner self-regulation
entries.notes: CNAF lists 'Inclusive Schooling' on its Nunavut page with text about Nunavut's inclusive schools but links to an old NWT page (ece.gov.nt.ca/fr/..., now 404); this is the Nunavut Department of Education's current inclusive education page (it also has information for parents and an autism resource for educators). CNAF's other Nunavut inclusive-education links (edu.gov.nu.ca) no longer resolve. The page's contact email is hidden.

entries.name: Rehabilitation Services (Nunavut Department of Health)
entries.description: Free physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech-language pathology and audiology from the Nunavut Department of Health for residents with a Nunavut Health Care Card, including for developmental delays and conditions. Services are based in Iqaluit and Rankin Inlet, with a visiting team for the Kitikmeot region and community therapy assistants in some communities; no doctor's referral is needed.
entries.cost_note: Free for Nunavut residents with a Nunavut Health Care Card.
entries.evidence: The Department of Health provides the following rehabilitation services free of charge to all Nunavut residents with a Nunavut Health Care Card:
entries.notes: Not from CNAF: added because Nunavut has fewer than 5 kept entries; no Nunavut autism society was found (autismnunavut.ca and .com do not resolve) and no separate Government of Nunavut disability services page was found. Phone is for the Baffin Region (Timimut Ikajuqsivik); Kivalliq (867) 645-8077, Kitikmeot (867) 983-4500. The Department of Health's Home, Community, and Continuing Care page (home care and respite for illness or disability) is another possible addition.

entries.name: Piruqatigiit Resource Centre
entries.description: An Iqaluit non-profit that offers Inuit-guided education, support and programs for Nunavummiut of all ages with suspected or confirmed FASD or other neurodiversities, and their families. Programs listed on its site include the Qaumajuut caregiver skills program, a monthly Qaggiq caregiver support group (also open across Nunavut through a private Facebook group), children's clubs, a siblings club and remote family support by phone or video.
entries.cost_note: The site does not mention cost.
entries.evidence: We are a nonprofit organization located in Iqaluit, Nunavut providing evidence-based, Inuit guided education, support and programming for Nunavummiut with FASD/other neurodiversities and their families across the lifespan.
entries.notes: Not from CNAF: added because Nunavut has only 4 checked services and no autism society. The children's and caregiver program pages were last updated in 2020 and 2021 and the calendar showed no upcoming events, so check which programs are running now. Email addresses on the site are hidden; use the phone or contact form. Funders listed: the GN Department of Health, Nunavut Tunngavik and the Government of Canada's Child First Initiative.

entries.name: Assessment Clinic (Piruqatigiit Resource Centre)
entries.description: A specialized clinic in Iqaluit with a psychologist, occupational therapist, speech-language pathologist and doctor who assess whether someone meets the criteria for an FASD diagnosis and/or other diagnoses. It does developmental assessments for children and youth aged 3 to 17 and some adults, and accepts self-referrals.
entries.cost_note: The clinic is funded by the Inuit Child First Initiative; the page does not mention a fee.
entries.evidence: At the clinic, the staff can conduct tests and determine if someone meets the criteria for an FASD diagnosis, and/or other diagnoses.
entries.notes: Not from CNAF: added because Nunavut has only 4 checked services. The referral or self-referral form is optional; completed forms can be dropped off at 1089F Mivvik St, Iqaluit. The page's email address is hidden, so only the phone is given; the page links a 2025 caregiver's guide to the clinic.

entries.name: Representative for Children and Youth's Office (Nunavut)
entries.description: An independent office, reporting to the Legislative Assembly of Nunavut, that makes sure Government of Nunavut programs and services meet the needs and rights of young Nunavummiut and their families. Anyone with a complaint about a department's service, or who cannot get a service for a young person or their family, can contact the office confidentially, even anonymously, for individual advocacy.
entries.cost_note: The site does not mention cost.
entries.evidence: If anyone has a complaint about a department's service, or is unable to receive a service for a young person and/or their family, they can bring it to the attention of our office for review.
entries.notes: Not from CNAF: added because Nunavut has only 4 checked services. It reviews services of Government of Nunavut departments and designated authorities. Toll free (and text) 1-855-449-8118; the office is on the 3rd floor of the Qamutiq Building, Iqaluit, and visits need an appointment.

entries.name: Kamatsiaqtut Nunavut Helpline
entries.description: A 24-hour, toll-free, anonymous and confidential telephone help line for Nunavut (and Nunavik), staffed by trained volunteers. It is for anyone who needs someone to talk to, not only people in crisis, including family members worried about someone; all volunteers speak English and many speak Inuktitut and French.
entries.evidence: Kamatsiaqtut is here for all people who need someone to talk to about their troubles, concerns, and anything that bothers you.
entries.notes: Not from CNAF: added because Nunavut has only 4 checked services. The Iqaluit number is 867-979-3333. Since 2015 Iqaluit volunteers take calls from 6 PM to 11 PM and the Distress Centre of Ottawa and Region takes them the rest of the day. Registered charity 868077546RR0001.

entries.name: Nunavut Human Rights Tribunal
entries.description: The territorial tribunal that resolves claims of discrimination or harassment in Nunavut under the Nunavut Human Rights Act, including discrimination based on disability. A person files a Notification form, orally or in writing and in any official language of Nunavut, within two years of what happened (family or community members can help); claims can go to mediation or a public hearing.
entries.cost_note: The site does not mention a fee to file; it suggests getting a lawyer where possible.
entries.evidence: If you believe that you have experienced discrimination or harassment in Nunavut, which has occurred within the last two years, you should contact the Nunavut Human Rights Tribunal.
entries.notes: Not from CNAF: added because Nunavut has only 4 checked services (other provinces' human rights commissions are already listed). It does not handle claims against federal businesses or organizations, which go to the Canadian Human Rights Commission (1-888-214-1090). The office is in Coral Harbour (PO Box 15); phone and fax are toll-free.
